To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The Taylor principle is still important in a model with asset prices and learning.

(i) the inclusion of asset prices in monetary policy is not desirable in terms of the E-Stable criterion; (ii) the inclusion of a weight on asset price misalignements does not improve the E-Stability properties of the optimal monetary policy rule; (iii) in an optimal rule, the weight on asset prices is small and the Taylor principle is important.

1) the Taylor principle remains crucial in the presence of asset price misalignment; 2) asset price misalignmments can be a source of instability in an adaptive learning framework; 3) asset price misalignment should not be included in a monetary policy rule in the context of an adaptive learning model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How does the introduction of asset price misalignment in a learning environment affect the optimal monetary policy?
the interaction between the conduct of monetary policy, asset prices and the formation of expectations.
the role of asset prices in the design and implementation of monetary policy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
asset price misalignements should be considered in the monetary policy framework only when the Taylor principle is satisfied.
the inclusion of stock prices in the monetary policy reaction function is not advisable.
the introduction of a response to stock price misalignments should be done with care and with a view to its potential effects on the stability of the learning process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asset prices do not play an important role in a learning framework.
asset prices are important, but that their introduction into monetary policy rules should be gradual and cautious.
the Taylor rule is still a very useful tool for central banks to conduct monetary policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in an adaptive learning environment, the introduction of asset prices in monetary policy rules may be destabilizing.
the introduction of stock price fluctuations does not necessarily imply a better performance of the economy.
the E-Stability approach is not a reliable tool to assess the robustness of a monetary policy rule in an environment where asset prices play a role.
